text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
GLOBES
- Stabilisation in unemployment level in third quarter -- 6.4 percent.
- The first Hanukkah in Israel with Dunkin' Donuts.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Justice Minister Tsachi Hanegbi weigh splitting attorney general's job in two -- one to advise the government, the other the country.
- Foreign contributors infuse $34 million into expansion of Jewish settlement in Negev, Golan and West Bank.
- Drop of 19.5 percent in number of tourists who arrived in October compared to same month last year.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- "It's time I met Arafat," Netanyahu says.
- Local authorities strike in all but big cities and towns.
- Worry in Israel Iran buys long-range missiles from Russia.
- European countries freeze new contracts with security industries.
- From next year: Professional Arabic required for grades 7 to 10 in Israel.
MAARIV
- "Time has come to meet Arafat," Netanyahu says.
- Judge Eliyakim Rubinstein the leading candidate for job of attorney general.
- Only a third of Israelis aged 21-51 do reserve duty.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. worried over future settlement drive.
- Local councils strike for promised funds.
- Bill to keep religious councils Orthodox passes first reading in parliament.
- Israeli army reveals undercover Egoz unit in Lebanon.
- Ultra-Orthodox Tel Aviv rally draws only a few Hassidic sects.
- Hanukkah doughnuts -- it's more than just eight days.
- January-September jobless rate down to 6.5 percent.
- Israel-Jordan upgrade treaty.
- Amir Paper may demand higher tariff on Pampers.
- Hapoalim, Clal Insurance to buy Atudot pension fund.
- Oil refineries expect gas shortage.
- United Mizrahi Bank's Yehuda Ofer: Data-purchase charges baseless.
- Bank Leumi Trust Co of New York net up 20 percent.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu: Time has come for a meeting with Arafat to finish the Hebron redeployment accord. Oman announces freeze of ties with present Israeli government.
- With support of Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert and Interior Minister Eli Suissa, Jewish building programme for Arab neighbourhood to be put to city planning and construction committee.
